title: Sequential Stopping and the Cost of Looking
model: Independent Bernoulli observations; simple null p0=0.5; fixed alternative p1=0.8
theorem: For a nonnegative likelihood-ratio martingale E_n with E_0=1 under the null, Ville's inequality gives P(sup_n E_n >= 1/alpha) <= alpha.
finding: The stopping rule is part of the statistical model: repeated observation is defensible only when the evidence process and stopping boundary are designed together.
limitations: Not a generic ML quality test.
Event audits only inspect recorded data.
